Review target: `24438c48..2f234371`

`high effort → 8 inline angles → dedup (no verify) → ≤10 findings`

You are reviewing for **recall** at high effort: catch every real bug a careful
reviewer would catch in one sitting. At this level, catching real bugs matters
more than avoiding false positives. Err on the side of surfacing.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (3 correctness angles + 3 cleanup angles + 1 altitude angle + 1 conventions angle, up to 6 each)

Run **8 independent finder angles** in sequence yourself, in THIS context — do NOT spawn subagents for them. Each
surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a one-line
`summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Reuse

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change fixes the root cause at the right depth rather than
patching a symptom with a fragile bandaid. Special cases layered on shared
infrastructure are a sign the fix isn't deep enough — prefer the simpler, more
general change to the underlying mechanism over adding special cases, and name
that change.

### Conventions (CLAUDE.md)

Find the CLAUDE.md files that govern the changed code: the user-level
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, the repo-root CLAUDE.md, plus any CLAUDE.md or
CLAUDE.local.md in a directory that is an ancestor of a changed file (a
directory's CLAUDE.md only applies to files at or below it). Read each one
that exists, then check the diff for clear violations of the rules they state.

Only flag a violation when you can quote the exact rule and the exact line
that breaks it — no style preferences, no vague "spirit of the doc"
inferences. In the finding, name the CLAUDE.md path and quote the rule so the
report can cite it. If no CLAUDE.md applies, return nothing for this angle.

Cleanup, altitude, and conventions candidates use the same
`file`/`line`/`summary` shape; in `failure_scenario`, state the concrete
cost (what is duplicated, wasted, harder to maintain, or which CLAUDE.md rule
is broken) instead of a crash. Correctness bugs always outrank cleanup,
altitude, and conventions findings when the output cap forces a cut.

Pass every candidate with a nameable failure scenario through — finders that
silently drop half-believed candidates are the dominant cause of misses.

## Phase 2 — Dedup only (no verify)

Pool all candidates. Dedup near-duplicates only (same defect, same location, same reason → keep one). Do NOT run verifiers; do NOT re-judge. Sort by severity.

## Output

Target **at least 5 findings**. If fewer genuine findings exist, emit what you have — do not invent to hit the floor.

Return findings as a JSON array of at most 10 objects:

```json
[
  {
    "file": "path/to/file.ext",
    "line": 123,
    "summary": "one-sentence statement of the bug",
    "failure_scenario": "concrete inputs/state → wrong output/crash"
  }
]
```

Ranked most-severe first. If more than 10 survive, keep the 10 most
severe. If nothing survives, return `[]`. Do not call the
ReportFindings tool even if it is available - this review's
output contract is the JSON block above.

-Storybook Controls and the CLI now list the DOM, ARIA and event attributes and a dependency's inherited props only where usage shows them: passed at enough of the component's call sites, read or forwarded by its body, or named by its props type (own, picked, required or defaulted). A plain `ComponentProps<'span'>` badge goes from 280 Controls rows to its 2 own props, and a button over Chakra UI's `ButtonProps` from 437 to 9. The rest are not lost: each is a name in its source's inheritance layer (`members`, with the ones the body reads in `used`). Storybook and the CLI now show the same rows. `htmlAttributes` still says which DOM attributes are known, not how many become rows; `collapseInheritedProps: 'none'` lists every resolved prop as before.
+Storybook Controls and the CLI now list a component's main props in full, plus the props the component itself uses, and leave large generated sets as names. Every prop of the component's props type and of the small interfaces it inherits from (Chakra's `loadingText`, `spinner`, `asChild`, `as`, `unstyled`, `css`, `variant`, `size`, the `html*` props) is a row, whether or not a story sets it. A DOM or ARIA attribute, or a style-system prop, becomes a row when the component's body reads it, destructures it or passes it on by name; spreading the props onto a DOM tag does not count. The hundreds of `@types/react` attributes and generated style props (Chakra's `SystemProperties` and conditions such as `_hover`) stay as names in their inheritance layer. A button over Chakra UI's `ButtonProps` goes from 437 Controls rows to 21, and a plain `ComponentProps<'span'>` badge from 280 to its 2 own props. `htmlAttributes` still says which DOM attributes are known, not how many become rows; `collapseInheritedProps: 'none'` lists every resolved prop as before.
diff --git a/docs/adr/0028-relevance-evidence-and-the-checker-scheduler.md b/docs/adr/0028-relevance-evidence-and-the-checker-scheduler.md
index 77aad671..01d783a4 100644
--- a/docs/adr/0028-relevance-evidence-and-the-checker-scheduler.md
+++ b/docs/adr/0028-relevance-evidence-and-the-checker-scheduler.md
@@ -45,8 +45,15 @@ Measured at de016f69 (`caliper-fixtures/oracle-run/diagnosis.md`): Storybook lis
 
 - **One placement, every lane.** `relevance::apply` keeps `decide`'s placement on the entry (`ComponentEntry::relevance`, not serialized) and lists by it (`relevance::narrow`); both checker merges call `narrow` again after laying out the checker's props, and take a `@types/react` prop only where the structural answer lists it (`react_prop_listed`), whatever the mode. A listed prop the placement leaves out moves to its source's layer as a name: the layer of its `parent`, else the element layer for an ambient source, else a new layer of that parent. A prop with no `parent` stays listed, so no name is lost.
 - **Scope.** Only props a source outside the project declares (a dependency's, React's or the DOM's, by declaring path) are narrowed; the project's own sources keep the collapse rule until a later slice measures them. `collapseInheritedProps: none` narrows nothing: it is the expanded view (`relevance: 'all'`).
-- **Rows.** A member passed at the call-site floor is a typed row even when ambient (a story needs its control; open question 2). An ambient member the body only reads is a `used` name. A member evidence puts forward that has no typed row (its source is collapsed) is named in `used`.
-- **Unknown evidence.** An ambient member with unknown body evidence is a name in its layer, not a row: without call sites a component lists its own and declared props, never a whole DOM source. A non-ambient member with unknown evidence is listed as before.
+- **Rows: the main props in full, plus what the component uses** (amended again 2026-11-16 after the owner clarified "use": "everything in the main props even if the story doesn't use them, and anything the actual component uses directly", not "used in a story"). `decide` lists a member as a typed row when:
+  1. the props type declares it itself (own, picked, overriding, required or defaulted); or
+  2. its source is an API source: neither ambient (by declaring path) nor large. A source is large when it reaches the component with more than `COLLAPSE_THRESHOLD` (30) members, counted per source over the answer's listed props (by `parent`) and its layers' members (`Member::large`). No story or call site is needed; or
+  3. the body reads it, destructures it (with or without a default) or passes it by name, or a spread onto a resolved component forwards it (that component's non-ambient props), whatever its source; or
+  4. it is passed at the call-site floor, which now only matters for members of ambient or large sources.
+
+  Everything else (the rest of `@types/react`'s and the shared DOM attributes, Chakra's `SystemProperties` and `Conditions`) is a name in its source's layer. A spread onto a DOM tag is no evidence. A body that hands its props on, or spreads onto a tag that did not resolve, promotes nothing and hides nothing: completeness no longer enters `decide` (`Body::handed_on` is gone). A row whose member the answer holds only as a layer name (a source the resolver collapsed) is named in that layer's `used` list, the only use `used` keeps. Story `args` are not read: Storybook already makes a control for every arg a story sets (`children` on the demo `Button`).
+
+  Why size, not the form of the type: Chakra's `Conditions` members come from `{ [K in keyof Conditions]?: V }`, but so do its recipe props (`ButtonVariantProps = { [K in keyof ButtonVariant]?: … }`, `size` and `variant`). The mapped-over-`keyof` form cannot tell the generated set from the API; the size of the key interface (130 against 2) can, so a rule on the form would add nothing a size rule does not decide. The threshold is the one the resolver already uses for ambient sources. A dependency API source of 31 to 200 members, which the resolver lists, is now a layer unless the body uses its members; the main-props differential on the corpora checks every source of 30 or fewer.
 - **Provenance, not names.** The placement keeps each left-out member with the source the structural answer gives it (`parent`, or the collapsed layer holding it); a merge narrows a listed prop only when name and source both match, so a same-named prop of another source is never hidden and a member with no structural source is narrowed in neither lane. A homomorphic mapped type's member (`{ [K in keyof Conditions]?: V }`) keeps its key's interface as `parent`, as the checker does.
 - **Declined key sets.** A `Pick` or `Omit` (in place or behind an alias) whose keys are not a closed set of string literals narrows no non-ambient source: which members reach is unproven (findings D5). Keys a `Pick` names through `Omit`, `Partial`, `Required`, `Readonly` or a project alias are picked.
 - **JSX children** pass `children` at a call site, after every attribute, as the JSX transform does; layout whitespace and empty expressions pass nothing.
